column1: On a scale from 1 (poor) to 10 (excellent), how would you rate the knowledge of economics of this judge?
On a scale from 1 (not important at all) to 10 (very important), how important is the use of economic reasoning in judicial decision-making for this judge?
On a scale from 1 (no use) to 10 (extensive use), to what extent does this judge use economic reasoning (economic concepts) to support their decision-making?
Do you consider that the use of economic reasoning by this judge has decreased, remained constant, or increased over time?

On a scale from 1 (negative response/effect) through 5 (no response/effect) to 10 (favourable response), do you consider that this judge responds favourably to parties’ arguments based on economic reasoning?

On a scale from 1 to 10, do you think this judge would consider that market regulators and supervisors contribute in a very negative (1), neutral (5), or a very positive (10) way to the functioning of the EU economy?

“Just because some rules (laws, regulations) are good for business does not mean they are necessarily good for fostering competitive markets.” On a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 10 (strongly agree), would this judge agree with the above statement?

“Regulations (laws) are necessary for the stability and efficient functioning of the economy.” On a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 10 (strongly agree), would this judge agree with the above statement?

“The economy is self-stabilising and government intervention is never (or almost never) required for an economy to attain an equilibrium.” On a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 10 (strongly agree), would this judge agree with the above statement?
